cohort: The study cohort consisted of 13,828 patients who underwent either vaginal or cesarean delivery from the First People's Hospital of Shangqiu and Henan Children's Hospital in China between February 1, 2018, and December 30, 2022.
finding: Elevated PM2.5 exposure is significantly correlated with an increased incidence of gestational hypertension and a decrease in neonatal birth weight.
mod_finding: PM2.5 exposure-related gestational hypertension was observed across both delivery modes, while oligohydramnios was specifically associated with higher PM2.5 exposure in the cesarean delivery group.
followup_time: Up to the neonatal period (approx. 28 days post-birth)
